title: Letter 17 — What Have I in Heaven?
attribution_note: Letter 17 of 46 in the collection Letters Sent — see Letter 1 for provenance.

pairs.en: *“My friend and brother in Christ!”*

Again there rings in my ears the song of David: *“Whom have I in heaven? and besides Thee what do I desire upon earth?”* [Psalm 72:25], O God? And I ask within myself, what does it mean? But my spirit gives this answer: the godly soul desires nothing, not only upon the earth but even in the heavens, save God. To her even heaven without God is nothing, as the earth also is nothing.

The ungodly and the lawless have their pleasures upon the earth: they have gold, silver, stones, diamonds, jacinths, horses, carriages, adorned houses and clothing of fine linen, and the rest of such things, and with these they comfort themselves. But the God-loving soul casts all this down with contempt and tramples it underfoot as refuse and mire; and she leaves not only the earth with its treasure, but heaven also, that she may find the one God, in whom she sets all her treasure and all her delight.

Nothing makes her glad: neither heaven nor earth, neither the things of earth nor the things of heaven, can comfort her, if she does not see Him whom she loves. As to a friend nothing is pleasant — whatever he sees, and with whomsoever he converses, and with whatever he is comforted — nothing of it is pleasant, if he does not see the beloved friend of his heart: so to the soul that loves God nothing can give comfort, if she does not see her Beloved. *“Whom have I in heaven? and besides Thee what do I desire upon earth?”* [Psalm 72:25], O God?

Let those who mind earthly things take comfort in the earthly [see Colossians 3:2]; let some be content with gold and silver, others with honour and glory, others with the wisdom of this age, others with luxury and sweet things, others with whatever other treasure is theirs. Let that be their comfort which they desire, which they count as treasure for themselves. None of this makes me glad; from all of it my heart turns away; and not only from that which is earthly, but even in heaven I seek and desire nothing save Thee, my God and my Creator! Thou alone art all things to me. In Thee alone I find all that I find not in all Thy creatures. I shall be content then, when I see Thee; I shall cease to desire then, when I find Thee; I shall be comforted then, when I come to Thee; then shall I *be satisfied*, when I *appear before Thy face*. *“O when shall I come and appear before the face of God?”* [Psalm 41:3]

Do thou also desire, O my soul, that One alone, and love the Desired, and seek the Beloved; and seek until thou find; seek while He may be sought and found. Thou hast no portion with the earth, thou who art heavenly. Thou art the image of God: seek the Prototype. For like tends to like: waters flow into the sea, earth returns to earth; birds keep with birds, and beasts with beasts, and cattle with cattle, and fishes with fishes, and man with man of his own kind — that is, the good with the good and the evil with the evil; and every thing seeks its like. Seek thou also Him to whom thou art like, and press toward Him as fire toward the height.

There is thy rest, and here thou shalt not find rest. Go through the whole world — thou shalt find nothing that will satisfy thee. Every thing finds rest in its own centre: the fish in the water; fire presses upward, toward its centre; cattle and beast rest upon the earth; air goes to air; the sojourner finds rest in his fatherland and in his own house.

Thou, O my soul, shalt not find rest for thyself here, in this world. All the beauty of this world is corruptible matter, vanity, corruption; the earth is all its preciousness. Thou art a spirit immaterial, immortal, and for thee there is no rest whatever in these things. For spirit does not rest in matter, but spirit finds rest in spirit. The earth with all its beauty, heaven with all its good order — these are bodies; they serve the body, content the body and give it rest. And with them thou hast no portion, and in them thou shalt not find rest, for thou art a spirit.

Heaven and the whole world will not satisfy thee, for there is no likeness between thee and the world. Turn, then, to thy Creator, who made thee after His own image. In Him alone thou shalt find thy rest, as in thine own centre. Say with the prophet: *“My soul cleaveth unto Thee,”* O God! *“Return unto thy rest, O my soul; for the Lord hath dealt bountifully with thee.”* [Psalm 62:9; 114:6] And mark well, O my soul, what David sings in that same place: *“They that remove themselves far from Thee,”* O God, *“shall perish”* [Psalm 72:27]. For he must perish who withdraws himself from life.

Behold for thee, brother, another song, which I have heard from the sweet singer David. Comfort thyself with it also, and remember me, a sinner, by it, that I too may sing from the heart: *“Whom have I in heaven? and besides Thee what do I desire upon earth?”* [Psalm 72:25], O God?
